definition: Conspicuous means easy to notice; standing out clearly from the surroundings in a way that attracts attention.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word conspicuous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know conspicuous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Wearing a bright orange raincoat in the middle of a gray, rainy city made her conspicuous from a block away.
A noticeable stain might catch your eye if you're looking closely; a conspicuous one draws attention on its own.
An obvious stain is impossible to miss even at a glance, and conspicuous goes a step further: it doesn't just fail to hide, it actively pulls the eye toward itself.

Prominent means standing out because of importance, rank, or position — a prominent lawyer, a prominent role. Conspicuous is about the eye: something stands out visually from its surroundings. A prominent citizen may dress plainly and never look conspicuous at all.

Eye-catching describes appealing looks that draw a pleased second glance — a poster or a dress designed to attract. Conspicuous is neutral about appeal: a stain, a blunder, or a bright coat can be conspicuous, standing out whether or not anyone enjoys looking.

Glaring describes what stands out harshly and unpleasantly, almost always a fault — a glaring error, a glaring omission. Conspicuous is milder and more general: it says something is easy to notice, without insisting the thing is bad.

During the stakeout, the rookie detective parked his shiny red convertible directly across from the suspect's building, a choice so conspicuous that the suspect noticed him within the hour and slipped out the back.
The bright, unusual car practically announced the detective's presence — nothing about it blended in, which is exactly what "conspicuous" means: impossible to miss.
Conspicuous is a fairly neutral, versatile word — it can describe something admirably eye-catching or something embarrassingly obvious, depending on context.
'Conspicuous by its absence' is a common set phrase for something so expected that its absence is itself noticeable.

Park rangers repaint the trail markers every spring, and they do not choose subtle colors.
A blaze must be conspicuous: hikers scanning a wall of green need one patch that refuses to belong to it.
